title: Ligustrazine attenuates high-fat diet-induced neurobehavioral deficits and hepatic dysfunction via modulation of the HO-1/Nrf-2/SIRT-1/PPAR-alpha axis.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究川芎嗪对高脂饮食诱导的NAFLD相关神经行为缺陷的改善作用，分子对接仅涉及小分子与蛋白受体，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a highly prevalent metabolic disorder that not only progresses to severe hepatic complications but is increasingly associated with neurological dysfunction, including cognitive impairment, anxiety, depression, and motor deficits. The present study investigated the neuroprotective and hepatoprotective potential of ligustrazine (LTZ) in a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced NAFLD-associated neurological dysfunction model in adult Wistar rats, with a mechanistic focus on SIRT-1, HO-1, Nrf-2, and PPAR-alpha signaling pathways. Molecular docking analyses demonstrated favorable binding of LTZ with SIRT-1, HO-1, Nrf-2, and PPAR-alpha receptors, suggesting its potential to modulate these targets. NAFLD and associated neurobehavioral deficits were induced by HFD administration for 35 days, followed by oral treatment with LTZ (80, 160, and 240 mg/kg) or pioglitazone (5 mg/kg) for an additional 35 days. LTZ treatment dose-dependently improved locomotor activity, motor coordination, depressive-like behavior, learning, and memory as assessed by open field, rotarod, forced swim, and Morris water maze tests. Biochemical and molecular analyses revealed that LTZ significantly restored antioxidant defenses, normalized lipid and liver enzyme profiles, reduced systemic and neuroinflammation, attenuated neuronal apoptosis, and corrected neurotransmitter imbalances in multiple brain regions. Furthermore, LTZ markedly upregulated SIRT-1, HO-1, Nrf-2, and PPAR-alpha levels in both liver and brain tissues, accompanied by histopathological and complete blood count profile improvement. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that ligustrazine effectively mitigates HFD-induced NAFLD-associated neurological dysfunction through multi-target modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and metabolic signaling pathways, highlighting its potential as a promising therapeutic strategy for NAFLD-related hepatic and neurobehavioral complications.
abstract_zh: 非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）是一种高度流行的代谢性疾病，不仅进展为严重的肝脏并发症，而且日益与神经功能障碍相关，包括认知障碍、焦虑、抑郁和运动缺陷。本研究探讨了川芎嗪（LTZ）在高脂饮食（HFD）诱导的成年Wistar大鼠NAFLD相关神经功能障碍模型中的神经保护和肝脏保护潜力，机制聚焦于SIRT-1、HO-1、Nrf-2和PPAR-alpha信号通路。分子对接分析显示LTZ与SIRT-1、HO-1、Nrf-2和PPAR-alpha受体具有良好的结合能力，表明其具有调节这些靶点的潜力。通过给予HFD 35天诱导NAFLD及相关神经行为缺陷，随后口服LTZ（80、160和240 mg/kg）或吡格列酮（5 mg/kg）治疗额外35天。LTZ治疗剂量依赖性地改善了开放场、旋转杆、强迫游泳和Morris水迷宫测试评估的运动活动、运动协调、抑郁样行为、学习和记忆。生化和分子分析显示，LTZ显著恢复抗氧化防御功能，正常化脂质和肝酶谱，减少全身和神经炎症，减轻神经元凋亡，并纠正多个脑区的神经递质失衡。此外，LTZ显著上调肝脏和脑组织中SIRT-1、HO-1、Nrf-2和PPAR-alpha水平，伴随组织病理学和全血细胞计数谱的改善。总体而言，这些发现表明川芎嗪通过多靶点调节氧化应激、炎症、凋亡和代谢信号通路，有效缓解HFD诱导的NAFLD相关神经功能障碍，突显其作为NAFLD相关肝脏和神经行为并发症有前景的治疗策略的潜力。
